classification.difficultyReason: Constructs triangles from three given side lengths using intersecting compass arcs; the available classification skill is an imperfect catalogue match.

content.prompt: Use a ruler and compasses to construct a triangle:

children.label: a
children.prompt: with side lengths $5\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$

answer.short: A triangle with sides $5\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$, retaining the construction arcs.
answer.worked: Draw $AB=10\text{ cm}$. With centre $A$ draw an arc of radius $5\text{ cm}$. With centre $B$ draw an arc of radius $8\text{ cm}$ intersecting the first arc at $C$. Join $AC$ and $BC$, retaining the arcs. Then $AC=5\text{ cm}$ and $BC=8\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Authored construction answer with intersecting compass arcs; no figure is supplied in the question.

children.label: b
children.prompt: with side lengths $6\text{ cm}$, $6\text{ cm}$ and $4\text{ cm}$

answer.short: An isosceles triangle with sides $6\text{ cm}$, $6\text{ cm}$ and $4\text{ cm}$, retaining the construction arcs.
answer.worked: Draw $AB=4\text{ cm}$. With centres $A$ and $B$, draw arcs of radius $6\text{ cm}$ meeting at $C$. Join $AC$ and $BC$, retaining the arcs. Both $AC$ and $BC$ are $6\text{ cm}$ because they are radii of the construction circles.

spec.description: Authored isosceles-triangle construction answer with intersecting equal-radius arcs.
